title: MITM · fixed-key preimage

target.description: 7-round AES-128 compression preimage with fixed public AES key. The figure has rounds0 through6, no final MixColumns, and terminal key addition.

setting.key_relation: One fixed public AES-128 master key and its standard key schedule.
setting.plaintext_model: One chosen 128-bit message; the public key/IV and full128-bit target are fixed.
assumptions: Unit-cost access to a large sorted table; native time is reduced-primitive computations.
All key bytes are fixed; Figure6 recovers the CGLSZ25 fixed-key construction.

time.note: Eqs4–7 include episode loops, key-path enumeration and matching; source-native reduced-primitive computation estimate.

data.note: Offline public compression problem; no secret oracle data collection.

memory.note: Source Table1/Figure path memory; not bytes, encryption counts or physical qubits.

preprocessing.note: No separately trusted precomputation exponent is extracted for this path.

success.description: The classical cost is an expected-solution MITM estimate; the source does not quantify a fixed-budget probability for the complete preimage event.

review.scope: PDF pp.17–18 Section5.1/Figure6; pp.4–6 fixed-key row and MMO definition. Algorithm1 whole-output condition and expected episode count checked.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.17–18 Section5.1/Figure6; pp.4–6 fixed-key row and MMO definition.
evidence.interpretation: Defining primary-text costs, output event and conditions checked together.
DDS Section5.1 explicitly reproduces this fixed-public-key preimage construction at the same time/memory exponents. The new source edition is retained without claiming a new improvement.

limitations: The complete named output probability is not quantified by the source.
